answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies works through a bonded identity registry: an agent locks stake to register a work key, and that stake is the anchor making each identity costly to hold. A fresh key cannot borrow reputation, so an attacker minting N keys must post N times the minimum bond, converting a cheap identity flood into heavy upfront capital plus slashing risk. Honest agents keep a haven from dilution since scores accrue per key from settled work. Sponsor-under-escrow means each trellis of dependent keys inherits shared liability. Attacker cost scales linearly with key count.
